messages:
mia: Heads-up — CI on main is failing intermittently with a unit test in serving. Seen this crop up across multiple linux runners: `tests/serving/test_kv_retry_backoff_non_deterministic.py::test_backoff`. Anyone grabbed this?
ci-bot: Build 2153 — FAIL
ci-bot: failing test: tests/serving/test_kv_retry_backoff_non_deterministic.py::test_backoff
ci-bot: log excerpt:
```
E   AssertionError: expected 3 retries, got 2
assert 2 == 3
```
arjun: I hit something similar yesterday when my local Docker NAT was congested. The retry timer drifted and the test's timing assertions flaked.
sam: Can you paste the full failing trace? is it always the same assertion or different parts of the test?mia: Full trace attached to CI, but the root is the backoff counter. Not always the same run — sometimes it passes. Triggered on linux-hosted runners primarily.lee: @arjun do you think network delay can change how KV cache invalidation + retry interplay behaves? sounds like the test races on response ordering.arjun: Yeah. The test assumes three retry attempts with precise intervals. If the response takes longer or a retry fires early due to scheduling jitter, the count assertion can be off. We saw this when Docker bridge had a transient delay.
mia: I'm going to kick a CI rerun now to see frequency. @ci-bot please rerun jobs for 2153.
ci-bot: Rerun queued for build 2153 (requested by mia).
ci-bot: Rerun started — build 2154.
ci-bot: Build 2154 — PASS
sam: Pass on rerun. So it's intermittent, not deterministic failure.
lee: My vote: make the test less timing-sensitive. Either poll with a timeout loop/assert eventually, or inject a fake clock so timing is deterministic.
arjun: Agreed. We can refactor the test to use a test-only clock interface. We already have a small TestClock in the runtime test utils that some suites use — we could reuse it.
mia: That sounds good. Short-term fix: relax the strict equality on retry count to allow >= 2 and <=3? Long-term: swap to TestClock.
sam: Also worth running full suite with --runslow on a stressed runner to try to reproduce more reliably before changing assertions.
lee: If we go TestClock route, add a follow-up for coverage so we don't regress into a timing assertion elsewhere.
arjun: I'll prototype a TestClock-based rewrite of that test and run it locally under a simulated slow network. If it stabilizes, I'll open a PR and link it here.
mia: Thanks. @sam can you do the stressed run this afternoon and tell us if you can make it fail more than once?
sam: Yep — scheduling a couple runs on a pinned worker now. Will report back by EOD.
ci-bot: Note: build 2155 queued (stressed-run by sam).
mia: If it looks like an infra flake (docker bridge), we should also file an eng-infra ticket to check runner network configs.
lee: Agreed. Tagging eng-infra if sam reproduces.
arjun: Plan: prototype TestClock change -> CI green on multiple runs -> PR -> migrate test. If infra reproduces, open infra ticket. I'll ping here with PR link.
mia: Super. Thanks team :thumbsup:
sam: Quick note — PR should reference #3421 (flaky-test tracker) when opened.
arjun: Will do. @mia I'll post the draft PR in this thread when ready.
mia: Closing this thread for now — tracking in #3421 and will follow up on PR.
